indicators.label: Net dwelling additions per year 2020–2026, per 1,000 inhabitants
indicators.note: Computed in scripts/build_net_dwellings.py into data/processed/net_dwellings.json. Both terms are published cells and the arithmetic between them is a difference, a division by the span in years, a division by population and × 1 000 — no trend, no cap, no model. The window years are resolved from BOL101 itself on every run, so the label must be rendered from meta.label_years rather than hard-coded. BOL101 counts dwellings that exist, not dwellings that are available: vacancy, second homes and student housing are not distinguished. The denominator is inhabitants, not dwellings, so this is not a growth rate of the stock. Denmark sits at +5.07 and one municipality (Ærø) is negative. Christiansø (411) reports 0 dwellings in BOL101 and has no value.
indicators.note_short: Net change in the dwelling stock 2020–2026, annualised — measured, not projected, and net of demolitions and mergers.
indicators.desc: (dwelling stock 1 January 2026 − 1 January 2020) ÷ 6 ÷ population × 1 000 — how many dwellings the municipality's housing stock actually gained per year over the window, per 1,000 inhabitants. Net, so demolitions, mergers and conversions out of housing are already subtracted; measured, not projected.
indicators.source: Danmarks Statistik BOL101 (dwelling stock, 1 January 2020 and 2026) and FOLK1A (population, latest quarter) — see docs/FORECAST.md §3
indicators.warn: History, not a forecast — this is what was built, not what will be. The window is six years rather than five because DST publishes no BOL101 for 2021 or 2022 (both closed over errors in the Building and Housing Register), so the change is annualised over the span that actually separates its two ends.

indicators.label: Reported crime · per 1,000 inh.
indicators.note: Denominator is resident population. City-centre areas with heavy daytime and night-time footfall (tourists, shopping, nightlife) score high because offences such as theft from person happen there, not because residents are unsafe — compare with Feeling safe (%), which is 90 % in Indre By. Place of offence (gerningskommune). Reported offences — reported ≠ solved. Excludes the traffic law. Series breaks: 2007 (police reform), 1 July 2013 (new definition of sexual offences), 2023 (~1,700 animal-welfare reports missing nationally). Not seasonally adjusted — hence rolling 4 quarters.

indicators.label: Open building cases on public buildings
indicators.note: Counts only cases with a permit (or case) date within the last three years; older open cases are listed separately in the area panel. Pilot coverage as for public_m2_per_1000.
indicators.desc: Public buildings with an open BBR building case whose permit is three years old or less.
indicators.source: BBR via Datafordeler (bygningens anvendelse 410–449), addresses and missing coordinates from DAR — see docs/PUBLIC_BUILDINGS.md
indicators.warn: An open case in BBR is owner-reported and is not a confirmed construction schedule: in the pilot only 1 of 290 open cases carried an expected completion date, and the median permit was 4.1 years old in København. Read it as case activity, not as a construction pipeline.

indicators.label: FP9 grade average
indicators.note: Pupil-weighted over folkeskoler and frie grundskoler that have a value; specialskoler are excluded because their intake makes an average meaningless. A school whose cell the source suppressed (under 3 observations, under 5 pupils for trivsel and the socioøkonomisk reference) is absent from the mean, not counted as zero — so an area's figure covers only the schools that publish. Copenhagen metro set only (19 municipalities).
indicators.note_short: FP9 bundne prøver, pupil-weighted; specialskoler excluded
indicators.desc: Weighted average of the bundne prøver at Folkeskolens Afgangseksamen (9th grade), latest school year, pupil-weighted over the schools of the area.
indicators.source: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk (STIL) — GS cubes KARA/KARAGNS (grades), OVER/OVERSKO (socioøkonomisk reference, klassekvotient), TRIV/TRIVIND (trivsel), ELEV/ELEVEX (elevtal); STIL institutionsregister for location and type. Kilde: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk — see docs/SCHOOLS.md
indicators.warn: A grade average is not a quality ranking — it mostly tracks intake. Read it next to the socioeconomic reference difference, which is what the source publishes it for.

indicators.label: Grade vs socioeconomic reference
indicators.note: Pupil-weighted over folkeskoler and frie grundskoler that have a value; specialskoler are excluded because their intake makes an average meaningless. A school whose cell the source suppressed (under 3 observations, under 5 pupils for trivsel and the socioøkonomisk reference) is absent from the mean, not counted as zero — so an area's figure covers only the schools that publish. Copenhagen metro set only (19 municipalities). Published one year behind the grades, so the latest school year usually has grades but no reference yet.
indicators.note_short: actual minus expected FP9 grade, pupil-weighted
indicators.desc: Difference between the schools' actual FP9 grade average and the socioeconomic reference — the grade the ministry's model expects given the pupils' background. Positive means the schools do better than their intake predicts.
indicators.source: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk (STIL) — GS cubes KARA/KARAGNS (grades), OVER/OVERSKO (socioøkonomisk reference, klassekvotient), TRIV/TRIVIND (trivsel), ELEV/ELEVEX (elevtal); STIL institutionsregister for location and type. Kilde: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk — see docs/SCHOOLS.md
indicators.warn: The difference is a model residual, not a causal claim about teaching. STIL marks per school whether it is statistically significant; most schools sit within the uncertainty band.

indicators.label: Pupil well-being
indicators.note: Pupil-weighted over folkeskoler and frie grundskoler that have a value; specialskoler are excluded because their intake makes an average meaningless. A school whose cell the source suppressed (under 3 observations, under 5 pupils for trivsel and the socioøkonomisk reference) is absent from the mean, not counted as zero — so an area's figure covers only the schools that publish. Copenhagen metro set only (19 municipalities).
indicators.desc: Generel trivsel, the overall indicator of the national pupil well-being survey (elevtrivselsmålingen), on a 1–5 scale. Pupil-weighted over the schools of the area.
indicators.source: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk (STIL) — GS cubes KARA/KARAGNS (grades), OVER/OVERSKO (socioøkonomisk reference, klassekvotient), TRIV/TRIVIND (trivsel), ELEV/ELEVEX (elevtal); STIL institutionsregister for location and type. Kilde: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk — see docs/SCHOOLS.md
indicators.warn: A self-reported survey with real non-response; the 1–5 scale compresses, so differences between areas are small by construction.

indicators.label: Pupils per school
indicators.note: Counts whole institutions, not departments: a school with several afdelinger is one school here. Copenhagen metro set only.
indicators.desc: Average number of pupils per school (folkeskoler and frie grundskoler) in the area, latest school year.
indicators.source: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk (STIL) — GS cubes KARA/KARAGNS (grades), OVER/OVERSKO (socioøkonomisk reference, klassekvotient), TRIV/TRIVIND (trivsel), ELEV/ELEVEX (elevtal); STIL institutionsregister for location and type. Kilde: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk — see docs/SCHOOLS.md

indicators.label: Young adults 20–34 vs Denmark 2026→2040
indicators.note: Computed in scripts/build_forecast.py from data/processed/forecast.json: the 2026 vintage of DST's municipal projection, ages folded into 0–5, 6–16, 17–19, 20–34, 35–64, 65–79 and 80+. Christiansø (411) is not a municipality and has no value. Never read together with Københavns Kommune's own forecast, which is a different run — see docs/FORECAST.md. Denmark here is the sum of the same 98 municipalities, not a separately rounded national table; it agrees with FRDK126's published age detail to 0.001 pp (scripts/validate_forecast.py check 5). Read it as a share-of-cohort map: a positive value is a municipality losing 20–34-year-olds more slowly than Denmark, which for most of the top ten is what is actually happening.
indicators.note_short: Measured against Denmark's own −7.1 %, not against zero — a positive value usually still means a shrinking cohort, just a slower one.
indicators.desc: The municipality's projected change in 20–34-year-olds 2026→2040 minus Denmark's, in percentage points. Denmark's own 20–34 population falls 7.1 % over the window, so only 7 of 98 municipalities gain any at all and the absolute map is almost uniformly negative; this one shows who holds young adults better or worse than the country.
indicators.source: Danmarks Statistik FRKM126 (municipal population projection, 2026 vintage), national control total FRDK126 — see docs/FORECAST.md
indicators.warn: A projection, not a measurement. DST's municipal projection assumes each municipality's recent fertility, mortality and migration behaviour continues; it carries no housing programme, so a large planned development does not appear in it.

Christiansø (411) is not a municipality and has no value. Never read together with Københavns Kommune's own forecast, which is a different run — see docs/FORECAST.md. The 98 values sum to Denmark's own change, −85 641 persons (scripts/validate_forecast.py check 5). Heavily skewed — København alone is a fifth of the national loss — so a linear diverging ramp needs clamping.
